newsitem.title: USA: Phelps Dodge misled investors, tribe alleges.
newsitem.headline: Phelps Dodge misled investors, tribe alleges.

text.p: Phelps Dodge Corp allegedly made misleading and false statements to shareholders about a long-running water rights dispute, an Apache tribe claimed in a letter to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday.
San Carlos Apache Tribe chairman Raymond Stanley asked the SEC to take "appropriate action" against the U.S. copper mining company.

The tribe and the mining company have battled for more than six years over water resources used by the company's copper operations at Morenci, Arizona. The Black River on the on the San Carlos Apache Reservation in Arizona is the source of an estimated 14,000 acre feet of water used annually by the mine.

In the letter, the tribe claimed Phelps Dodge published misleading information about the dispute in its annual report to shareholders issued last month. The report said the company and the tribe were involved in discussions over the company's right to use a pump station located on Apache land and to transport water to the mining complex.
"There have been no negotiations of any kind whatsoever since July 23, 1996," the tribe said in its letter.
Phelps Dodge was scheduled to hold its annual shareholders meeting on Wednesday in Phoenix.
